findings.title: Unsafe access to possibly undefined destinationCalendar element
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined` if the array is empty, but the next line accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without an optional chain or null check, causing a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") whenever no destination calendar exists for the event (e.g., falling back to default calendar). This will throw at runtime for the common case of a user without a destination calendar set.

findings.title: createEvent passes credential.id as externalId-unrelated 3rd param inconsistently
findings.body: createEvent in CalendarManager now accepts an optional `externalId` parameter and passes `credential.id` as the calendar's createEvent `credentialId` parameter, but the resulting `externalId` field in the EventResult is just whatever was passed in by the caller (often undefined when called without it, e.g. for non-traditional/other_calendar paths and the fallback path). This means `referencesToCreate` built from `result.externalId` in EventManager.ts will often be `undefined`, silently losing the destination calendar's externalId in those paths which previously worked via `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`. This could cause the correct calendar to not be updated when later referencing it.

findings.title: N+1 DB queries fetching credentials per destination calendar
findings.body: Inside createAllCalendarEvents, for every `destination` in `event.destinationCalendar` with a `credentialId` not already present in `this.calendarCredentials`, a separate `prisma.credential.findUnique` call is issued inside the loop. For events with many hosts/destination calendars, this results in many sequential DB round trips instead of batching with `findMany`, significantly increasing booking creation/update latency. The same pattern is repeated in updateAllCalendarEvents (lines ~516-541).

findings.title: loadUsers organization slug field dropped for dynamic bookings
findings.body: The original query for dynamic event bookings selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` on top of userSelect.select. The rewritten loadUsers function in the `!eventTypeId` branch omits `organization` from the select entirely, so `users[].organization` will be undefined downstream (e.g. when building org-aware links or redirects for dynamic bookings), silently breaking that feature path.

findings.title: loadUsers falls back incorrectly when eventType.hosts is empty for non-dynamic events
findings.body: When eventTypeId is set and `eventType.hosts` is empty/undefined, the function returns `eventType.users` directly without mapping in `isFixed`, unlike the hosts branch which always sets `isFixed`. Downstream code (e.g., ensureAvailableUsers) relies on `isFixed` property; falling back silently without it may cause assumptions elsewhere (`isFixed` undefined) to behave differently than before, where `eventType.users || []` was used but callers may expect isFixed consistently set after this refactor given the surrounding logic changes with COLLECTIVE host handling.

findings.title: teamMemberPromises destinationCalendar collection happens as a side effect inside map, order not guaranteed with Promise.all
findings.body: teamDestinationCalendars.push(...) is performed as a side effect within the async map callback passed to users.slice(1).map, then awaited via Promise.all. Because the push happens synchronously before the async getTranslation resolves, order is fine, but if any promise in the array rejects, partially mutated teamDestinationCalendars will already contain some calendars leading to inconsistent state on partial failure. More importantly, destination calendars for non-collective team events are silently dropped (not pushed) but every team member's email/name truthfully still gets added as an attendee — review whether skipping calendar aggregation for ROUND_ROBIN was intentional, since those hosts' destination calendars won't receive the event either, which seems to defeat part of the PR's purpose of supporting multiple hosts generally.

findings.title: destinationCalendar connect only uses first calendar when booking multiple hosts' calendars
findings.body: After building `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (potentially containing several hosts' destination calendars for collective events), the Prisma booking creation only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` to the booking's single `destinationCalendar` relation. This means only the first host's destination calendar reference is persisted on the Booking record, even though createAllCalendarEvents will create events on all hosts' calendars. Subsequent updates/cancellations relying on `booking.destinationCalendar` (a single relation) will only ever see one calendar, breaking calendar sync during reschedule/cancel for the other hosts, since those flows build `destinationCalendar` as `[booking.destinationCalendar]` (single) throughout other files (handleCancelBooking.ts, confirm.handler.ts, etc.).

findings.title: updateEvent calendar lookup logic is broken: compares externalId to itself
findings.body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (due to the ternary), meaning this find will always compare each `cal.externalId` against a falsy `externalCalendarId`, which will never match any valid calendar externalId. Effectively, when no externalCalendarId is explicitly passed, `selectedCalendar` always resolves to `undefined`, silently breaking calendar id resolution rather than falling back to the destination calendar's externalId as likely intended (e.g., previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). Same issue appears in deleteEvent (line ~317).

findings.title: Error swallowed silently without logging in updateAllCalendarEvents catch block
findings.body: The removed `console.error(message)` call in the catch block of updateAllCalendarEvents means errors during calendar update are no longer logged anywhere before being converted into a resolved (non-throwing) promise, making failures harder to diagnose in production.
